subject: OrbitalAI — Private GPU sizing & operational scenarios
messages:

Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@orbitalai.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask: private GPU runbook & throughput targets

Elliot —

Thanks for the time last week. OrbitalAI is moving a subset of inference traffic to a private VPC deployment with Redwood and we need to lock down sizing and an operational scenario matrix before the procurement window next month. High-level asks:

- Target sustained throughput we should plan for (RPS and tokens/sec) across three phases: POC, ramp, steady-state.
- Recommended headroom and warm-pool sizing (percent over expected peak).
- Network egress and overlay constraints to call out to our infra team.
- Failure-mode behaviors and the graceful degradation story (e.g., fall back to hosted model variants).

Context: expected peak concurrent model sessions ~1800, avg request = 120 tokens, 95th p95 latency requirement <= 350ms for the majority of calls. We can be flexible on model family — primary is an LlamaX-13B variant.

Can you drop a short operational scenarios doc so we can align with our infra and procurement?

Cheers,
Matt
Matthew Harris
Head of ML Infrastructure, OrbitalAI

Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private GPU runbook & throughput targets

Matt —

Thanks for the context; appreciate the traffic profile. I sketched three operational scenarios below (POC / Ramp / Steady-State) with suggested GPUs, warm-pool %, and network guidance. This is intentionally conservative on headroom so we have buffer during cutover. Please share with infra and let us know which scenario you'd like us to model in a runbook.

Summary (high level):
- POC: 4x A100-80GB (1 shard), target sustained 75 RPS, warm-pool 20% — used for functional validation and failover exercises.
- Ramp (3 months): 12x A100-80GB (3 shards), target sustained 300 RPS, warm-pool 35% — autoscale policy conservative, warm-pool to reduce cold KV cache misses.
- Steady-state: 24x A100-80GB (6 shards) or equivalent Ampere family mix with quantization recommended, target sustained 700–900 RPS depending on batching, warm-pool 40% — aim for p95 generation latency <= 350ms.

Notes:
- The RPS above assumes average request = 120 tokens and batching window tuned to 15–30ms for moderate latency-sensitive workloads.
- If OrbitalAI can accept token-quantization (4-bit) and slightly relaxed top-k sampling, we can reduce GPU footprint ~30% in steady-state.
- Network: plan for 10–12 Gbps egress per shard (encrypted), plus cross-region replication headroom if you want active/standby.

Action items:
1) Laura — can you add a short network checklist (NIC oversubscription, MTU, switch buffer guidance, flow-control) and attach to runbook?
2) Marissa — confirm commercial options for a committed slab vs graduated autoscale for the Ramp window.
3) Matt/Sandeep — decide which scenario to model in the ops-runbook; we can run a short bench to validate p95.

I'll put a one-page scenario summary into the shared Drive. Attaching a quick draft.

–Elliot
Elliot Price
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private GPU runbook & throughput targets

Folks —

Quick network checklist (top items to validate with your infra team):

1) NIC and SR-IOV mapping: map 2 physical NICs per rack to avoid single-switch failure, enable SR-IOV for inference containers if using host-based NIC pass-through.
2) MTU: 9000 (jumbo frames) recommended across the path to reduce CPU overhead on large KV/cache transfers.
3) Switch buffers and congestion: ensure at least 2MB buffer per port for jumbo frame flows; test with synthetic burst traffic at 1.5x expected peak for 10s windows.
4) Egress caps: provision per-shard egress at 12 Gbps and a cluster-level reserve of 25% for replication and telemetry spikes.
5) L4 load balancer health probes: prefer TCP health checks and a two-tier drain policy to avoid dropping KV cache during evictions.
6) MTLS termination: keep end-to-end encryption; offload only at dedicated TLS proxies if using HSMs for key mgmt.

Failure mode guidance:
- If a shard fails, traffic should be routed to a warm standby with degraded throughput; provide graceful throttling to downstream services and optionally fallback to Redwood hosted variant for best-effort continuity.

Attached a short checklist PDF with links to our internal runbook sections for on-prem fabric verification.

Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Matt —

From a commercial standpoint we can offer two lanes for the Ramp window:

A) Committed slab (12-month): guaranteed 12x A100 equivalent, 20% prefunded warm-pool credits, runs at a reduced unit rate.
B) Graduated autoscale: pay-as-you-go with committed minimum (3 months), built-in burst credits for first 30 days of ramp to absorb variability.

Recommend Committed Slab if you expect predictable growth and want cost predictability. We can include one scheduled bench validation and two post-cutover tuning sessions as part of the onboarding package.

Also attaching a short workbook (xlsx) with slot-to-QPS conversions, assuming the LlamaX-13B baseline. This will help you map expected concurrent sessions -> GPU shards.

Marissa Cole

2) Redwood to run a focused bench on your staging network (we need a 2-hour maintenance window) to validate p95 on the Ramp configuration (12x A100 equiv). ETA for bench run: 2028-07-11 — I'll schedule once Matt confirms maintenance window.
3) Infra checklist: Matt to share contact for network ops; Laura's checklist attached (network-path-checklist.pdf) is the primary input.

If you confirm Ramp, we'll model warm-pool 35%, target sustained ~300 RPS and a burst headroom up to 500 RPS for 30s windows. We'll also include a fallback policy that shifts 15% of traffic to a hosted Redwood variant if latency breaches p95 > 450ms during cutover.

Matt — happy to hop on a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the runbook contents if helpful.

Best,
